use_case: Augment printed media with volumetric content
note: Scope: "Volumetric video content with object audio". Object audio is sound positioned in the scene.

use_case: Reconstruct a live event at a remote viewing site for its audience, with life-size images, spatial sound and lighting
note: Scope: "with sound coming from where the performers appear". Sound positioned at the performers.

use_case: Join a meeting in a real room remotely through the room's live 360-degree video
note: Scope: "receives the room's sound spatially". Room sound rendered spatially for the remote participant.

use_case: Carry vibrotactile signals as numbered channels of the audio stream, each assigned to an actuator position
note: Scope: "travel as additional channels of the audio stream". Vibration carried in the audio stream.

use_case: Guide prospects through multi-user XR showrooms of battery production plants (Matthews, VISHOW)

use_case: Carry a digital asset into another virtual world and have it look and behave the same

use_case: Generate a digital human from a user's images or 3D model through an IEEE 3079.3.1 service broker
note: Scope: "downloads the resulting digital human". The result is an avatar body the application shows.

use_case: Take an avatar into a virtual world on another platform, keeping its appearance, identity and the assets it carries
note: Scope: "The avatar keeps its appearance". The avatar's appearance travels.

use_case: Create an avatar that looks, sounds and moves like the user from their own video, voice and preferences, with generative AI
note: Scope: "a portrait-true appearance". A generated avatar body.

use_case: Visit the same virtual world from any device through a web browser, with scale, behaviour, avatars and interaction kept consistent
note: Scope: "avatar appearance and animation". The avatar looks the same on each device.

use_case: Drive an avatar's face and body in real time from the user's own expressions and movement
note: Scope: "through a small set of expression units (eye opening, mouth opening)". An expression standard between camera and avatar.

use_case: Create an avatar that looks, sounds and moves like the user from their own video, voice and preferences, with generative AI
note: Scope: "maps voice to lips, expression and posture". Expressions and visemes the avatar carries.

use_case: Produce a video in which an AI-driven 3D digital human presents a given text
note: Scope: "keeps lips and speech in step". Visemes driven from speech.

use_case: Take an avatar into a virtual world on another platform, keeping its appearance, identity and the assets it carries
note: Scope: "the user's identity". The avatar stays bound to its user's identity.

use_case: Generate a level-of-detail chain for a real-time asset
note: Scope: "for skinned characters, a reduced skeleton". Reduced representations of a character.

use_case: Capture a performer's motion to animate a digital character
note: Scope: "streamed in real time onto a character". Motion of one body played on another is retargeting.

use_case: Drive an avatar's face and body in real time from the user's own expressions and movement
note: Scope: "which need not match the user's proportions". Motion mapped onto a different body.

use_case: Carry a digital asset into another virtual world and have it look and behave the same
note: Scope: "translated to the target's rigging and format". Rigging translates only where bone naming and structure agree.

use_case: Carry a digital asset into another virtual world and have it look and behave the same
note: Scope: "(an avatar, a wearable, a vehicle, an instrument) moves from the world that holds it into a different world".

use_case: Design, present and sell fashion as digital garments
note: Scope: "Garments are ... sold for avatars". Items worn by an avatar are wearables.

use_case: Enter any virtual world with one self-owned personal manifest, disclosing to each only the data it needs
note: Scope: "avatar, apparel and accessories". Worn items that travel.

use_case: Capture a real place or object volumetrically so it can be revisited after it changes
note: The capture is registered in time and place, for example a site before works or an as-built condition. Registration in time across repeat captures is time-varying capture.

use_case: Broadcast a live event volumetrically to viewers who choose their own viewpoint
note: Scope: "each viewer chooses their own viewpoint within it instead of receiving a director's cut". A viewpoint no capture camera occupied is novel view synthesis.

use_case: Generate 3D content with AI assistance from existing data or a description
note: Scope: "3D assets ... are generated with AI assistance ... The result is placed in the virtual world".

use_case: Guide visitors through 14 AR stations on a city's history and towers (Rottweil)
note: Scope: "sees 360-degree panoramas from them".

use_case: Watch a live sports event remotely through immersive camera views the viewer selects
note: Scope: "a 360-degree panorama stitched in real time from cameras at the venue". Panoramic imagery of the scene.

use_case: Join a meeting in a real room remotely through the room's live 360-degree video
note: Scope: "a meeting held in a physical room that a 360-degree camera captures". The room is shared as panoramic video.

use_case: Start one 360-degree film on every headset in a seated audience at the same moment
note: Scope: "the same 360-degree film". A full panoramic view carried as media.

use_case: Show prospective apprentices the training and customer centres in 360-degree VR at apprenticeship fairs (AOK Baden-Württemberg)
note: Scope: "filmed on two shooting days". The centres are shown as 360-degree film.

use_case: Replace a cancelled world trade fair with a virtual brand world of 16 theme planets, guided tours, adviser chats and a 24/7 live stage (Häfele Discoveries)
note: Scope: "133 360-degree rooms". The rooms are panoramic images.

use_case: Capture a real place or object volumetrically so it can be revisited after it changes
note: A real place or object is captured volumetrically and registered in time and place. Point cloud encoding is the interchange format that registration and later revisiting depend on.

use_case: Build a spatial model of a production area from existing data
note: A point-cloud scan of the existing hall is one of the inputs the model is assembled from.

use_case: Review BIM, CAD and point cloud models in AR through mixpace with server-side rendering (HoloLab)
note: Scope: "open BIM, CAD and point cloud models in mixpace".

use_case: Stream ship laser scans merged with retrofit designs to AR headsets for design review (ShipReality)
note: Scope: "merges billion-point laser scans of a vessel with its CAD retrofit designs".

use_case: Scan existing stations into building twins and use them for capacity analysis and AR inspections (Deutsche Bahn)
note: Scope: "the point cloud and mesh become the building twin".

use_case: Plan plants on a scanned virtual factory in three phases (BMW Group, Omniverse)
note: Scope: "capture a plant with 3D scanners into a photorealistic model". Proposed: the scope does not say whether the scan is carried as points or as a mesh.

use_case: Capture a real place or object volumetrically so it can be revisited after it changes
note: The captured state can be revisited after the original has changed or gone. Revisiting a captured moment is volumetric playback.

use_case: Represent a person volumetrically so they appear present at a distance
note: Scope: "represented volumetrically ... captured, reconstructed and placed in the receiving space". A captured, time-varying person carried as media.

use_case: Broadcast a live event volumetrically to viewers who choose their own viewpoint
note: Scope: "A live event is broadcast volumetrically to many viewers".

use_case: Preserve ephemeral and living culture so it can be experienced later
note: Scope: "performances ... movement-based traditions ... are captured with their context, so that the public can experience them after the event". Proposed: the scope does not name the capture method.

use_case: Augment printed media with volumetric content
note: Scope: "Volumetric video content ... is attached to a printed page".

use_case: Generate 3D content with AI assistance from existing data or a description
note: Scope: "scenes are generated with AI assistance from ... a natural-language description".

use_case: Train on a stationary bike while riding through a virtual world generated from the workout, with intensity targets and the group's performance on screen
note: Scope: "turns the workout's data into a route through a 3D world". A 3D place generated rather than reconstructed.

use_case: Enforce a creator's entitlement when a digital asset changes hands
note: Scope: "The terms a creator set for their asset are applied to any transfer of it". A grant checked at the moment of use or transfer.

use_case: Settle a creator's entitlement on chain when a tokenised asset changes hands
note: Scope: "the creator's entitlement is settled by the contract that governs the token". As 0027, on chain.

use_case: Enter any virtual world with one self-owned personal manifest, disclosing to each only the data it needs
note: Scope: "access credentials and tickets". Grants checked at entry.

use_case: Run a player-organised game tournament whose prize pool a smart contract holds and pays out
note: Scope: "entry fees and prizes held and paid out by a smart contract". Payments authorised and settled by the contract.

use_case: Reward players' contributions to a game community with tokens they can spend or cash out
note: Scope: "exchange for money". Tokens converted to money; the payment exchange is implied.

use_case: Publish a game or experience made on a platform, and earn from the players who use it
note: Scope: "in a platform currency that can be converted to money". Players pay and creators are paid in the platform currency.

use_case: Find content held on other metaverse platforms through one discovery service, preview and buy it, and publish a mash-up of it
note: Scope: "their own platform buys it on their behalf". A platform pays on the user's behalf.

use_case: Promote a product on virtual street signage that takes the visitor into the brand's store on another platform, and sell it there
note: Scope: "buys and pays through a payment provider". A payment exchange from inside the world.

use_case: Have an object designed in a virtual world manufactured, and keep the delivered product synchronised with it
note: Scope: "orders its manufacture through a commerce system". The order is paid from the virtual world.

use_case: Order the repair of a physical object from the anomaly its digital twin reports in a virtual world
note: Scope: "The user chooses a shop and pays". A payment exchange from inside the world.

use_case: Establish and present verifiable provenance or ownership of an asset
note: Scope: "When the asset changes hands, the new holder is recorded". A record binding holder, asset and time; receipts are one form of it.

use_case: Promote a product on virtual street signage that takes the visitor into the brand's store on another platform, and sell it there
note: Scope: "receives a purchase confirmation with a delivery date". A record of the purchase.

use_case: Verify an automated driving function against simulated traffic scenarios with measurable coverage, in ASAM OpenSCENARIO
note: Scope: "The same scenario files run unchanged on different compliant tool chains". Running unchanged on any compliant tool chain presumes a shared conformance test.

use_case: Protect a user from harassment in a virtual world through a safety patrol, and keep an offender out of other platforms through shared reputation
note: Scope: "judge conversations and actions against the platform's rules". Review against the platform's rules.

use_case: Publish a manufacturer's products as planning-ready 3D objects with master data, so that planners can place, show and order them in their own planning tools
note: Scope: "checked against the industry's data standard". A named contract the content declares it meets.

use_case: Record a work procedure step by step on a phone, mark it with AR symbols, and share it as a guide anyone can open by link
note: Scope: "the author updates the guide and everyone has the new version". Shipping a change to every reader.

use_case: Publish a manufacturer's products as planning-ready 3D objects with master data, so that planners can place, show and order them in their own planning tools
note: Scope: "kept current". Shipping changes without breaking planners' content.

use_case: Explore augmented content as a group by projecting it from a handheld device onto the surroundings
note: Scope: "projects content registered to the walls, floors and objects it points at". Content is fixed to the place it belongs to.

use_case: Record a work procedure step by step on a phone, mark it with AR symbols, and share it as a guide anyone can open by link
note: Scope: "AR markers such as warning symbols and arrows placed where they belong". Content fixed to a place.

use_case: Guide a worker through checking and completing orders on a head-mounted display while a collaborative robot brings and removes the boxes
note: Scope: "marks the shelf compartment of a missing item". The mark has to stay on one compartment of a real shelf; the scope does not say how it is anchored.

use_case: Present location-based learning content across a site in augmented reality
note: Scope: "attached to specific real-world locations across a site ... visitors ... discover it on a mobile device". Content fixed to a place across devices and sessions.

use_case: Keep one shared map of a real site up to date from the AR devices that use it, so that any device can locate itself in it
note: Scope: "content placed by one user appears at the same real position for every other". Shared, persistent anchors.

use_case: Inspect a factory with live sensor readings shown on the machines, from high- and low-resource AR devices that share one map of the site (ETSI ARF)
note: Scope: "registered at the real sensors". Dials registered to real positions in a shared map.

use_case: Install connected devices by anchoring each one's twin at its real position, so that it can be found and operated by pointing at it
note: Scope: "anchored at the device's real position with an AR device and shared with every user who needs it". An anchor that persists and is shared across users.

use_case: Maintain a city-scale digital twin for planning and service delivery
note: The representation spans terrain, buildings, infrastructure and networks, maintained across many departments and data owners. Many owners contributing one spatial model is exactly where coordinate reference systems have to agree and do not.

use_case: Capture a real place or object volumetrically so it can be revisited after it changes
note: The capture is registered in place as well as in time. Registering a capture in place across systems is a coordinate reference system problem.

use_case: Plan the radio coverage of a room from a map built with an AR device
note: Scope: "the borders of each door and window the technician points at are added". A structured description of an interior space.

use_case: Keep one shared map of a real site up to date from the AR devices that use it, so that any device can locate itself in it
note: Scope: "which is merged into the global map, so the map follows objects that have moved". Map lifecycle: partial maps merged and kept current.

use_case: Make an invisible or measured phenomenon visible in place
note: Scope: "registered to the physical place it describes", naming networks and subsurface assets. For those the place is a position on the Earth. Proposed, because a registration can also be local to one device.

use_case: Involve residents in a planned development before it is built
note: Scope: "in their own surroundings and at street level, from any viewpoint". Placing a planned wind park in a resident's view needs its pose against the Earth.

use_case: Guide a driver along a route with an immersive navigation overlay
note: Scope: "presented from the driver's point of view, rendered from geospatial mapping data". The view is a pose against the Earth.

use_case: Lead hikers and cyclists along a literary AR route with hotspots and local offers (Günter Grass-Haus, Tour de Grass)
note: Scope: "follows a 32 km route ... opens 24 AR hotspots". Hotspots along an outdoor route are found by position on the Earth. Proposed: the positioning method is not named.

use_case: Share a trip with people at home while it happens, by placing the travellers' geo-tagged media in a virtual world they can walk through
note: Scope: "the content is geo-tagged". Content placed by real-world position.

use_case: Play a game in the real world with other players, with virtual objects placed at real locations
note: Scope: "registered to real places by satellite positioning, compass and camera". Objects placed by geospatial pose.

use_case: Save and share a persistent address of a place, viewpoint and moment in a virtual world, and return to it later
note: Scope: "tie a physical place to its digital overlay". A real place expressed against the Earth.

use_case: Guide a blind or visually impaired pedestrian through their surroundings with spoken and vibration cues from sensed obstacles, location tags and recognised landmarks
note: Scope: "RFID tags at street corners give the exact position". Position expressed against the street.

use_case: Maintain a city-scale digital twin for planning and service delivery
note: The use case keeps a city-scale digital representation current enough to plan with and deliver services from. City-scale delivery to a client is tiled terrain and city streaming.

use_case: Command an operation from a shared virtual operational picture
note: Scope: "Commanders see an operation in real time on 3D maps". 3D maps of an operating area are streamed geospatial data. Proposed: tiling is not named.

use_case: Plan a Liebherr crane lift with real-time load and ground-pressure checks on a drone-scanned site (Liebherr Crane Planner)
note: Scope: "a 3D model of the real site from drone scans or Google Maps data". Map-provider 3D data arrives as streamed tiles. Proposed: the format is not named.

use_case: Run and maintain an intralogistics fleet of vehicles, robots and people
note: Scope: "Tracked people and robots are monitored ... recorded tracks can be rolled back". Recorded tracks are pose series.

use_case: Record workers' movements in a captured workshop twin and analyse ergonomics and walking time (Mercedes Field Services)
note: Scope: "records workers' movements during maintenance ... in that 3D space" and "times the walk from point A to point B". A recorded movement is a pose series. Proposed: the record may store positions only.

use_case: Fly an autonomous drone across a city to deliver goods, under a delivery contract and the airspace authority's live approval
note: Scope: "the drone's position, arrival time and compliance data go to an air-traffic channel". A live pose stream shared with the authority.

use_case: Recreate a recorded real-world traffic situation as a simulation scenario, and vary it
note: Scope: "each actor's lateral and longitudinal movement becomes a concrete scenario". Recorded pose series become the scenario.

use_case: Test how future users experience and find their way through a planned space by observing them in a VR replica before it is built
note: Scope: "their movement paths, gaze, wayfinding". Movement paths recorded and compared across participants are pose series; the frame is not stated.

use_case: Map the energy use and emissions of road traffic segment by segment from recorded trips on a city's digital twin
note: Scope: "computed from recorded trips of fleets and phone users". A recorded trip is a series of positions over time.

use_case: Record an airport's flight movements automatically and link each to its noise and emissions on the airport's digital twin
note: Scope: "captured from the aircraft's own position messages". Position messages of aircraft are streams of poses, replayed as tracks.

use_case: Keep one shared map of a real site up to date from the AR devices that use it, so that any device can locate itself in it
note: Scope: "with which another device finds its own pose without knowing where it started". Relocalisation against a map is visual positioning.

use_case: Measure a tracking method's registration error, speed and robustness against the ground truth of a trial set
note: Scope: "its estimated camera poses are compared with the dataset's ground truth". The method under test recovers pose from camera imagery.

use_case: Run and maintain an intralogistics fleet of vehicles, robots and people
note: Scope: "robots' planned actions and safety zones are shown to workers". Identified zones with events scoped to them.

use_case: Produce citizen-sourced sensor evidence to ground a local policy debate
note: Scope: "traffic counts by mode and speeds ... anonymous aggregates are published to a public dashboard and API". Summaries with a spatial and temporal meaning. Proposed: zones are not named.

use_case: Check a planned structure against the protected airspace around a runway in a 3D model
note: Scope: "the obstacle limitation surfaces around an airport's runways". Protected 3D zones against which a structure is tested; whether they are published for others to use is not stated.

use_case: Establish and present verifiable provenance or ownership of an asset
note: Scope: "presents this to a party that has to rely on it". The relying party needs the evidence behind the claim, not only the claim.

use_case: Control who may access personal data, and license it on the owner's terms
note: The owner decides who may reach the data and on what terms, and those terms are enforced. The Atlas defines this capability as "what a subject may do, readable by a party that did not issue it", a permission grant that crosses a boundary.

use_case: Resolve who may open which part of a shared 3D asset
note: Scope: "a decision is made at the moment of each request about who may open which part". What a subject may do, read by the party that holds the part.

use_case: Edit one 3D scene simultaneously with others in a browser-based engine
note: Scope: "roles separate viewing, editing and deploying". A permission grant. Proposed: inside one product it need not be readable by another party.

use_case: Keep a personal social space in a virtual world that friends on other platforms visit through portals
note: Scope: "sets who may enter and what each visitor sees". Permissions a visiting platform must read.

use_case: Identify and authenticate an IoT device that roams across metaverse platforms, through a shared trustworthy identity store
note: Scope: "authorises and performs its services for the device". What the device may do in the receiving metaverse.

use_case: Control who may access personal data, and license it on the owner's terms
note: Scope: "consent, purpose, duration, revocation". These are the parts of the Atlas definition of consent carried with the subject, almost word for word.

use_case: Enter any virtual world with one self-owned personal manifest, disclosing to each only the data it needs
note: Scope: "consents". Consent carried with the user.

use_case: Establish a verified identity or compliance status once and reuse it elsewhere
note: The use case establishes a property of a person or organisation once: identity, age, sanctions status or professional standing. That property has to be expressed in some form a second party can read; the Atlas calls that the credential format.

use_case: Accumulate a reputation in one place and carry it to another
note: The standing has to arrive in a form the receiving place can rely on. Reliance by a party that did not observe the conduct is the credential problem, whatever the payload happens to be.

use_case: Enter any virtual world with one self-owned personal manifest, disclosing to each only the data it needs
note: Scope: "with verifiable credentials or zero-knowledge proofs". Verifiable claims about the user.

use_case: Establish a verified identity or compliance status once and reuse it elsewhere
note: The result is reused by later platforms. Reuse across a platform boundary is a request-and-present exchange.

use_case: Identify and authenticate an IoT device that roams across metaverse platforms, through a shared trustworthy identity store
note: Scope: "each side retrieves and verifies the other's identity there, they authenticate each other". Presenting and verifying identity between parties.

use_case: Establish a verified identity or compliance status once and reuse it elsewhere
note: The result is reused without disclosing the underlying documents. That is selective disclosure stated as a requirement, not an option: the use case is not satisfied by a credential that leaks the passport.

use_case: Control who may access personal data, and license it on the owner's terms
note: The owner sets consent, purpose, duration and revocation. Consent scoped by purpose is selective disclosure with a time bound on it.

use_case: Enter any virtual world with one self-owned personal manifest, disclosing to each only the data it needs
note: Scope: "presents only the items that experience needs". Selective disclosure.

use_case: Have a device's or a player's data processed for several metaverses by external services, with every exchange recorded on trustworthy storage
note: Scope: "the records of the data exchange are kept on tamper-resistant shared storage for audit". A verifiable record of what was exchanged.

use_case: Control who may access personal data, and license it on the owner's terms
note: Licensing is possible where the owner permits it. Licence terms that have to be acted on at the point of use are what the Atlas calls rights enforcement.

use_case: Enforce a creator's entitlement when a digital asset changes hands
note: The creator's terms are applied to a transfer of the asset wherever the transfer happens. That is rights enforcement at the point of use, across a boundary the creator does not control.

use_case: Combine lifecycle data from several organisations without any of them losing control of it
note: Scope: "The combined data answers queries while each part stays under its contributor's terms." Terms acted on at the point of use are rights enforcement.

use_case: Settle a creator's entitlement on chain when a tokenised asset changes hands
note: Scope: "the creator's entitlement is settled by the contract that governs the token, not by the venue". Licence terms acted on at the point of transfer.

use_case: Establish a verified identity or compliance status once and reuse it elsewhere
note: A claim about a subject needs a subject. The scope says "a property of a person or organisation", and that person or organisation is the base identifier the Atlas calls the identity root.

use_case: Accumulate a reputation in one place and carry it to another
note: The reputation attaches to an identity, and the record says so by invoking VW-UC-0024. A standing with nothing to attach to does not travel.

use_case: Hold a learner's immersive training progress as NGSI-LD context, and query how it evolved
note: Scope: "an identity alias on the agent joins the identifiers different platforms use for one learner". One base identity behind several platform identifiers.

use_case: Identify and authenticate an IoT device that roams across metaverse platforms, through a shared trustworthy identity store
note: Scope: "keep their identities in a shared trustworthy storage". A base identifier for a thing, held across metaverses.

use_case: Accumulate a reputation in one place and carry it to another
note: A standing earned in one place is presented somewhere else that did not observe it. The Atlas capability is named "Reputation and social graph" and defined as "portable relationships and standing": the same idea seen from the other side.

use_case: Protect a user from harassment in a virtual world through a safety patrol, and keep an offender out of other platforms through shared reputation
note: Scope: "The sanction is recorded with a reputation service". Standing that travels between platforms.

use_case: Establish a verified identity or compliance status once and reuse it elsewhere
note: Scope: "The result can expire and be withdrawn." A withdrawn result has to be discoverable by every platform that reuses it: credential status and revocation.

use_case: Establish a verified identity or compliance status once and reuse it elsewhere
note: Scope: "the result is reused by later platforms without repeating the check". A later platform has to know which issuers to accept.

use_case: Call people outside a virtual world from inside it, by phone, message or video, without revealing anyone's contact details
note: Scope: "so neither side's number or identity is exposed". Contact without disclosing identifiers.

use_case: Rehearse a radiological incident response in a real room, with the sources, the contamination and the decontamination overlaid in augmented reality
note: Scope: "a tracked, simulated spray". A tracked handheld device drives the simulation.

use_case: Control a virtual camera, virtual objects and effects in a mixed reality scene with a person's tracked hand gestures
note: Scope: "a touchpad, a controller". Handheld device input.

use_case: Take trade-fair visitors on a virtual e-car drive across Europe, steered with tracked charging plugs, to show how few charging stops it needs (EnBW Energy Drive, IAA 2021)
note: Scope: "steering with two real charging plugs tracked by HTC VIVE". Tracked handheld objects as controllers.

use_case: Collaborate on one spatial model across sites and devices
note: Scope: "different device classes (browser, desktop VR, standalone headset)". Serving each class means learning what the client can do. Proposed: the scope names the classes, not the discovery.

use_case: Provide access services within an immersive experience
note: Scope: "interoperability with assistive devices". The experience has to learn what the user's device can do. Proposed: the scope names interoperability, not discovery.

use_case: Visit the same virtual world from any device through a web browser, with scale, behaviour, avatars and interaction kept consistent
note: Scope: "the experience adapts to what the device can do". The world learns what the client device can do.

use_case: Learn human anatomy by exploring a 3D body model layer by layer, on a headset, tablet or desktop
note: Scope: "available in VR, AR or on a desktop". One model on several kinds of device.

use_case: Rehearse ECMO set-up and therapies on XENIOS device twins and a virtual patient in a virtual ICU, on phone, web or in VR with hand tracking (Fresenius Medical Care Heart and Lung app)
note: Scope: "on iOS, Android, Windows, in the browser, or in VR". One application on several kinds of device.

use_case: Let residents compare variants of an urban development on a big screen, on tablets and in VR at the same time (Bauhaus Participation Lab Weimar, Consensive VR4more)
note: Scope: "each on the device that suits them: a big screen, a tablet or a VR headset". One session serving different devices needs to know what each can do.

use_case: Let teachers create VR learning content from templates without coding and give it to classes in VR or on laptops and phones (MilleaLab, SHINTA VR, Indonesia)
note: Scope: "on a standalone headset or, without VR, on a laptop or Android phone". The same content runs with or without VR, so the viewer must learn what the device can do.

use_case: Measure a user's gaze and attention in an immersive environment for research or evaluation
note: Scope: "An immersive session is instrumented with eye tracking".

use_case: Guide a machine operator along computed work lanes in their field of view
note: Scope: "any input is given by gaze or voice".

use_case: Let people experience eye diseases while playing table tennis in VR (ZEISS)
note: Scope: "eye tracking adjusts the simulated impairment to their gaze in real time".

use_case: Control a virtual camera, virtual objects and effects in a mixed reality scene with a person's tracked hand gestures
note: Scope: "gaze dwell". Gaze as input.

use_case: Test how future users experience and find their way through a planned space by observing them in a VR replica before it is built
note: Scope: "their movement paths, gaze, wayfinding". Gaze recorded as data, with the privacy constraints that go with it.

use_case: Capture a performer's motion to animate a digital character
note: Scope: "A performer's full-body movement is tracked ... and streamed in real time". Body pose delivered as a live sensor stream.

use_case: Drive an avatar's face and body in real time from the user's own expressions and movement
note: Scope: "capture the user's facial expression and body movement". Face and body tracking as input.

use_case: Control a virtual camera, virtual objects and effects in a mixed reality scene with a person's tracked hand gestures
note: Scope: "A depth camera tracks the skeleton of a person". Body pose as a live input stream.

use_case: Manipulate a molecular structure in 3D for scientific research
note: Scope: "manipulate molecules and proteins ... with hand gestures".

use_case: Train cabin crew safety procedures in an A340 cabin in VR booths with a virtual trainer (Lufthansa Aviation Training)
note: Scope: "using their hands".

note: Scope: "with injuries, cries and smells". Smells in a VR scene need a scent effect delivered with it; the scope does not say how they are produced.

use_case: Reconstruct a live event at a remote viewing site for its audience, with life-size images, spatial sound and lighting
note: Scope: "the media are adapted to the site's screens, projectors, loudspeakers and lights". Venue lighting reproduced on whatever lights the viewing site has; light is one of the row's effects, though the scope may mean stage lighting only.

use_case: Render the sensory effects authored with media content on the effect devices a viewer actually has, adapted to their capabilities and the viewer's preferences
note: Scope: "a description of sensory effects: wind, light and flashes, scent, fog, heat, vibration, the movement of a motion seat". The row's definition: effects described by intent and adapted to the devices present.

use_case: Ride a VR experience on a seat that moves in step with the content
note: Scope: "while the seat tilts and shakes in step with what the film shows". Motion-seat movement synchronised with the content.

use_case: Provide access services within an immersive experience
note: Scope: "subtitles ... multilingual and contextual help". Legible text in three dimensions.

use_case: Learn human anatomy by exploring a 3D body model layer by layer, on a headset, tablet or desktop
note: Scope: "reading labels". Text in three dimensions.

use_case: Represent a person volumetrically so they appear present at a distance
note: Scope: "placed in the receiving space". The receiving side has to render the volumetric representation it is sent.

use_case: Examine a patient's CT or MRI images as a 3D volume in a headset, slicing and annotating it for teaching or case discussion
note: Scope: "shown as a volume in three dimensions". Volume rendering.

use_case: Record and replay a work sequence
note: Scope: "The motion of a person ... is captured in the model and replayed for analysis". Stored and replayed motion is animation encoding.

use_case: Produce a video in which an AI-driven 3D digital human presents a given text
note: Scope: "the facial and body animation". Generated animation clips.

use_case: Learn human anatomy by exploring a 3D body model layer by layer, on a headset, tablet or desktop
note: Scope: "following animations of function". Stored animation clips.

use_case: Stream a very large 3D model to a standalone headset or mobile device at continuously adaptive level of detail, without preprocessing or a render server
note: Scope: "loads only the parts and the detail the current view needs". Selecting parts before their geometry is loaded needs bounding volumes; the scope does not say how parts are selected.

use_case: Learn human anatomy by exploring a 3D body model layer by layer, on a headset, tablet or desktop
note: Scope: "showing and hiding structures". Named sets of structures as targets for an operation.

use_case: Let trade-fair visitors walk through a full-scale virtual substation and inspect its transformers and monitoring systems on a guided tour in three languages (Nexans Morocco, Metaenga)
note: Scope: "open layered views of the technology". Showing the substation layer by layer needs named sets of objects as targets.

use_case: Compose one digital twin from several authoring tools without a master file
note: The parts are not flattened into a single master file that one tool owns; they reference one another and each stays editable in its own tool. That is composition by reference with overrides, stated as the requirement.

use_case: Find content held on other metaverse platforms through one discovery service, preview and buy it, and publish a mash-up of it
note: Scope: "combine content into a mash-up and publish it". Content from several sources composed into one scene.

use_case: Author or convert 3D content for reuse across immersive applications
note: Scope names "packaging" and ends "with a reusable result". A reusable packaged result is an asset container, and the use cases that invoke this record each expect to open it.

use_case: Export a validated concept to the engineering systems that build it
note: Scope: "exported as something the next system can act on (geometry for the CAD system ...)". The handover is a file the receiving tool opens.

use_case: Deliver a CAD-derived model to a web viewer as glTF
note: Scope: "the result is exported as glTF or GLB for a WebGL viewer".

use_case: Make a patient-specific 3D model from medical images, to print an implant or a surgical planning aid
note: Scope: "stored as it is used by the printers, STL or OBJ with its materials and textures". The asset container travels as it is.

use_case: Plan hotel and cruise-ship interiors from imported architects' plans to photorealistic renderings with custom materials (GH Hotel Interior Group, Palette CAD)
note: Scope: "imports architects' plans". Models carried between tools.

use_case: Let teachers create VR learning content from templates without coding and give it to classes in VR or on laptops and phones (MilleaLab, SHINTA VR, Indonesia)
note: Scope: "from templates and 3D models without coding". Teachers bring 3D models into the authoring tool; the format is not stated.

use_case: Find and enter a specific place or experience across virtual worlds
note: Entering an experience held in another virtual world can mean travelling there or hosting it, as a running experience with its own logic, inside the visitor's world. The scope does not choose; containment is the second way.

use_case: Author or convert 3D content for reuse across immersive applications
note: The use case converts, reduces and retopologises content, starting from CAD, scan or authored geometry. Converting between geometry representations is the whole subject of the record, and geometry encoding is what it converts between.

use_case: Let an AI agent query and act on engineering 3D data
note: Scope: "navigate a product structure". The product structure is the scene graph the agent walks.

use_case: Validate physical parts against virtual ones with a measurement arm in AR (Volkswagen, instant3Dhub)
note: Scope: "load assemblies directly from PDM with their structure".

use_case: Resolve who may open which part of a shared 3D asset
note: Scope: "parts of a composed 3D asset belong to different owners with different terms". The terms have to travel with each part to be decided on.

use_case: Propose, review and merge a change to shared 3D product data
note: Concurrent work by several parties converges instead of being overwritten. Several parties on shared product data is where rights and licence metadata has to travel with the asset.

use_case: Produce and distribute media with portable rights, metadata and identity
note: Scope: "creators' rights ... stay intact and portable across platforms".

use_case: Author or convert 3D content for reuse across immersive applications
note: Scope names "materials" in the list of what conversion has to carry across.

use_case: Record a physical defect in three dimensions on the twin of the asset that carries it
note: Scope: "recorded where it actually is, in three dimensions, on the digital twin". A defect record is structured data attached to one part of the scene. Proposed: the scope does not say the record travels to another system.

use_case: Produce and distribute media with portable rights, metadata and identity
note: Scope: "metadata ... stay intact and portable across platforms".

use_case: Let an AI agent query and act on engineering 3D data
note: Scope: "read and write properties". Structured properties attached to parts of the model.

use_case: Validate physical parts against virtual ones with a measurement arm in AR (Volkswagen, instant3Dhub)
note: Scope: "with their structure and metadata".

use_case: Produce furniture from the planning model, with parts lists, labels and machine data generated without re-entering anything
note: Scope: "the bill of materials, the part labels". Domain data carried with the model.

use_case: Publish a manufacturer's products as planning-ready 3D objects with master data, so that planners can place, show and order them in their own planning tools
note: Scope: "with their master data". Domain data carried with the 3D object.

use_case: Plan and carry out electricians' customer jobs in an authentic virtual building, scored on function and profit (FOSH, South Africa)
note: Scope: "in a BIM-based virtual building". A BIM model carries the domain properties (materials, components) the job is planned and costed from.

use_case: Travel to a chosen place in a virtual world on an automatically planned route, with a smooth camera that keeps the view clear
note: Scope: "along a route that keeps clear of obstacles". Navigable space for path planning.

use_case: Create or edit 3D design geometry while immersed in it
note: Scope: "modelling native CAD surfaces ... the result is kept in the authoring tool's own format". Exact surfaces carried in mathematical form.

use_case: Tessellate engineering CAD geometry into a mesh at a chosen density
note: Scope: "The surface geometry of CAD models ... is converted into a polygon mesh at a density chosen". The Atlas definition: carried in mathematical form "so a receiver can evaluate or tessellate them".

use_case: Deliver a CAD-derived model to a web viewer as glTF
note: Scope: "the geometry is tessellated at high density". Tessellating exact CAD surfaces.

use_case: Work on geometric designs together in persistent 3D spaces of the 3DConcepts tool on instant3Dhub (BMW Group)
note: Scope: "collaborate live on JT-Open and STEP AP242 data". STEP AP242 carries exact geometry in mathematical form.

use_case: Produce furniture from the planning model, with parts lists, labels and machine data generated without re-entering anything
note: Scope: "cuts the parts exactly as designed". Exact geometry carried to the machine.

use_case: Establish and present verifiable provenance or ownership of an asset
note: Scope: "establishes that an asset is what it claims to be". A record of who made an asset and how is what such a claim rests on.

use_case: Propose, review and merge a change to shared 3D product data
note: The change and its approval remain traceable afterwards. Traceable authorship of a change is provenance.

use_case: Produce and distribute media with portable rights, metadata and identity
note: Scope: "content authentication ... stay intact and portable". Authentication of content is a signed record of who made it.

use_case: Create participatory art with audiences and stakeholders
note: Scope: "with the provenance of digital works tracked".

use_case: Make a patient-specific 3D model from medical images, to print an implant or a surgical planning aid
note: Scope: "its version history". Where the model came from and how it changed travels with it.

use_case: Compose one digital twin from several authoring tools without a master file
note: One coherent digital twin is composed from parts authored in several different tools. Parts from several tools become coherent only if transforms and coordinate conventions agree.

use_case: Review a product design in immersive 1:1 scale before physical prototyping
note: Scope: "reviewed immersively at 1:1 scale". Judging proportion and reach at 1:1 only works if the imported design arrives at its real-world size.

use_case: Author or convert 3D content for reuse across immersive applications
note: Scope names "units, orientation" explicitly. Units and scale is the capability, and the fact that a conversion use case has to name it at all is the evidence that it is not settled.

use_case: Build a spatial model of a production area from existing data
note: A dimensionally trustworthy model is assembled from a 2D floor plan, CAD assemblies, a point-cloud scan or a catalogue of standard objects. Dimensional trust across four source kinds is units and scale.

use_case: Try a planned layout at full scale before committing to it
note: Scope: "walked at 1:1 scale ... whether a walkway is wide enough". A width judged by walking it is only right if the units are.

use_case: Preview a product placed in the customer's own environment using augmented reality
note: Scope: "to judge its fit". Fit is judged only if the model arrives at real size.

use_case: Explain a complex product's inner workings with a full-scale interactive hologram
note: Scope: "shown ... as a full-scale hologram built from its CAD data".

use_case: Show trade-fair visitors the cabin forward of a full-size eVTOL side wall in AR (Diehl Aviation)
note: Scope: "sees, at true scale, everything forward of it in the real air taxi". Content meeting a physical wall at true scale needs real-world units.

use_case: Visit the same virtual world from any device through a web browser, with scale, behaviour, avatars and interaction kept consistent
note: Scope: "Environment scale". Scale stays the same on every device.

use_case: Test how future users experience and find their way through a planned space by observing them in a VR replica before it is built
note: Scope: "built at true scale from its BIM or CAD models". Real-world scale carried from the building models.

use_case: Hold and compare variants of a layout
note: Scope: "kept as first-class, switchable objects". Named, selectable alternatives of one configuration are the Atlas's variants.

use_case: Keep a configurable product's part database optimised for any configuration with InstaLOD (Accenture Song)
note: Scope: "hundreds of part variants ... assembled into any configuration". Named alternatives with a selection mechanism; the parent VW-UC-0157 does not name variants.

use_case: Complete clay design models with mixed reality overlays (Porsche, Meyle+Müller and medialesson)
note: Scope: "switch geometric variants, colours, animations ... over it".

use_case: Show a client their planned room photorealistically and in variants before it is built, so that they can decide
note: Scope: "in several variants of layout, surfaces and materials". Selectable variants of the design.

use_case: Publish a manufacturer's products as planning-ready 3D objects with master data, so that planners can place, show and order them in their own planning tools
note: Scope: "in all variants". Selectable variants of each product.

use_case: Let residents compare variants of an urban development on a big screen, on tablets and in VR at the same time (Bauhaus Participation Lab Weimar, Consensive VR4more)
note: Scope: "compare the variants of a planned urban development". Named alternatives of the plan, selected for comparison.

use_case: Test how future users experience and find their way through a planned space by observing them in a VR replica before it is built
note: Scope: "design variants are compared under the same conditions". Selectable alternatives of the design.

use_case: Examine a patient's CT or MRI images as a 3D volume in a headset, slicing and annotating it for teaching or case discussion
note: Scope: "Medical image data (DICOM, CT, MRI)". Image stacks carried as a volume.

use_case: Preview a product placed in the customer's own environment using augmented reality
note: Scope: "places a 3D model of a product ... into their own real environment". Placing on a real surface asks the runtime where that surface is.

use_case: Find and configure products online, fit out a vehicle in 3D and preview a water softener in WebAR (Würth)
note: Scope: "places a configured water softener in their own room with WebAR". Placing on a real floor asks the runtime where it is.

use_case: Show special foundation machines at work on virtual construction sites in AR (Liebherr AR Experience)
note: Scope: "points a tablet at an architectural model, or at any free surface". Placing on any free surface is a hit test against the real world.

use_case: Draw people to a venue or an event with an augmented reality scene on their own phone
note: Scope: "anchored in the person's surroundings". Placing a scene on the surfaces of a room or a street needs intersections with the sensed surroundings.

use_case: Lead Parisians from key installations across the city to a new store with an augmented reality key, and open a virtual showroom on arrival (H&M Home)
note: As its parent VW-UC-0439, whose function this record performs in one named organisation.

use_case: Turn a viewer's room into a scene of a horror event from a code in a streaming advertisement (Universal Halloween Horror Nights)
note: As its parent VW-UC-0439, whose function this record performs in one named organisation.

use_case: Show invited guests the park's landmark tower above them in a web AR invitation before the opening (Universal Epic Universe)
note: As its parent VW-UC-0439, whose function this record performs in one named organisation.

use_case: Make a gargoyle break out of the park's entrance arch on guests' phones (Universal Halloween Horror Nights)
note: As its parent VW-UC-0439, whose function this record performs in one named organisation.

use_case: Augment printed media with volumetric content
note: Scope: "a reader pointing a smartphone or headset at the page sees the content appear on it". Recognising an image and reporting its pose.

use_case: Keep one shared map of a real site up to date from the AR devices that use it, so that any device can locate itself in it
note: Scope: "Each AR device that moves through the place maps what its camera sees". Each device reconstructs what it sees.

use_case: Plan the radio coverage of a room from a map built with an AR device
note: Scope: "the walls' planes are derived from the tracked pose and intersected into the shape of the room". The device reconstructs the room it is in.

use_case: Explain a complex or hidden product feature in place using augmented reality
note: Scope: "The product is tracked so that the overlay stays registered to it". Tracking a product to keep an overlay on it is usually done from its model; the scope does not say how.

use_case: Compare a manufactured part with its CAD model through a markerless AR overlay on a tablet
note: Scope: "registered to the part by model-based tracking, without markers or preparation of the part". The row's definition, word for word.

use_case: Show workshop technicians animated repair data on the car through a tablet (Porsche PARiS)
note: Scope: "which is recognised by its silhouette". A known object recognised from its shape, not from a marker.

use_case: Complete clay design models with mixed reality overlays (Porsche, Meyle+Müller and medialesson)
note: Scope: "place missing parts precisely on a physical design model". Registering parts to a clay model needs its pose; the scope does not say how it is found.

use_case: Paint or project new surfaces onto a physical object, and keep them in place as the object is moved
note: Scope: "an optical tracker follows the object so the imagery stays on it when it is moved". A physical object of known geometry tracked so content stays registered to it.

use_case: Show what the virtual world knows about a physical object on a user's AR glasses when they select the object
note: Scope: "selects the object or an area". The glasses must recognise the physical object to show its data on it.

use_case: Keep a person near the machine visible through an augmented reality overlay
note: Scope: "where a person or object would be hidden behind graphics, the overlay is removed or opened at that point". Virtual content giving way to the real.

use_case: Train incident commanders for a mass casualty incident in a free-roam VR market scene (MATHILDA)
note: Scope: "walks freely through a 25 by 15 m VR scene". Free roam depends on the usable physical area the runtime reports.

use_case: Snorkel freely through a virtual underwater world in a pool, wearing a waterproof VR snorkel mask
note: Scope: "the system keeps track of the pool edges". The usable physical area is bounded.

use_case: Walk through a virtual world along a guided trail in a tracked arena, balancing over narrow paths and bridges
note: Scope: "walks on their own feet through a tracked arena". The physical area bounds the virtual trail.

use_case: Produce citizen-sourced sensor evidence to ground a local policy debate
note: Scope: "processing on the device so that no images leave it; anonymous aggregates are published". Disclosure controls on sensed data.

use_case: Keep a person near the machine visible through an augmented reality overlay
note: Scope: "The machine's near field is scanned in real time, and where a person or object" is found. Naming what a real object is.

use_case: Guide a blind or visually impaired pedestrian through their surroundings with spoken and vibration cues from sensed obstacles, location tags and recognised landmarks
note: Scope: "the service can name the landmark the person is facing". Naming what a real object is.
